data.title: Data centres to double Malaysian electricity demand by 2050
data.description:
MALAYSIAN electricity demand is set to more than double through 2050 due to a rapid buildout of power-hungry data centres.

Energy needs will rise to 49.8 gigawatts by mid-century from 22.5 gigawatts in 2027, the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation said on Thursday (Nov 26).

Data centres will account for 21 per cent of power demand by 2050, up from 11 per cent in 2027, the ministry said.

The South-east Asian nation has ambitious plans to be a regional hub for artificial intelligence.

It’s drawn billions of dollars of investment from tech heavyweights including Oracle, Amazon.com and Alphabet’s Google, which plans to spend US$15 billion to expand data centre and cloud operations in Malaysia over the next two years. 

Tighter US restrictions on access to technology could hinder Malaysia’s plan, however.

Concerns that Nvidia chips are being smuggled to China via South-east Asia has prompted Washington to blacklist some companies in the region, with Malaysia pledging to tell data centre operators not to host, lease space or provide services to the firms.

The country is considering replacing some of its coal fleet with nuclear power to meet the growing demand, although that isn’t slated to happen until 2040.

Malaysia announced plans this month to launch a separate wholesale electricity market for large power consumers including data centres, to safeguard supply for households and factories. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Consumer protection panel proposes cooling-off period for prepaid packages, higher cap on small claims
data.description:
[SINGAPORE] Consumers could have a mandated period to reconsider their expensive prepaid packages and cancel without penalty if recommendations by a panel are taken up by the Government.

The panel, which was tasked to review Singapore’s consumer protection regime, said consumers who may have come under undue sales pressure should have a window to reconsider after leaving the shop. It suggested rolling this out in high-risk sectors, naming the beauty and wellness sector as a priority.

Announcing its proposals on Nov 27, the panel also recommended more influencer advertisement transparency and stronger ticketing protection. It submitted its seven recommendations to the Government on the same day.

This is the first comprehensive review of Singapore’s consumer protection regime since the last major amendment to the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act in 2018, said the panel’s co-chair Melvin Yong, who is president of the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE).

Should the recommendations be approved, more consumers could also take their disputes to court.

The panel suggested that the Small Claims Tribunal (SCT) increase its standard limit for consumer claims to S$30,000, up from S$20,000 currently. THE STRAITS TIMES

data.title: Asean equities in for a ride in 2027; Singapore, Vietnam favoured: JPMorgan
data.description:
[SINGAPORE] Singapore and Vietnam are the two Asean equity markets JPMorgan Chase analysts are “overweight” on, even while the region is expected to face headwinds in the first half of 2027.

This comes as economists expect three more rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve – in January and March 2027, on top of December this year.

US dollar strength will rise with the move, and “pressure” emerging market currencies too, noted a Thursday (Nov 26) report.

“Almost all Asean central banks would deliver rate hikes over the next few months to stymie inflation and defend their currencies,” said the analysts.

“This is done in an environment where the fiscal budgets have limited room for growth support...(such that) earnings growth might remain under pressure.”

For Singapore equities, the JPMorgan analysts stand by their earnings quality and dividend visibility, especially with substantial “fiscal support” on top of the ongoing Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP), which is expected to boost market liquidity in early 2027.

Launched in February 2025, the EQDP is Singapore’s S$6.5 billion equity market stimulus programme, with S$5.4 billion allocated to three groups of fund managers so far. A fourth tranche of fund managers will be appointed in 2027.

Others are less bullish on the city-state’s equity market moving into 2027, however. Citi analysts earlier put an “underweight” rating on the Singapore market relative to others in the Asean region.

Morgan Stanley analysts also said there is an “incremental negative from an investor risk perception” for Singapore, along with Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia, after news of fresh tariffs and a freeze on Nvidia chip shipments to the four countries, a Friday report by The Business Times indicated.

They noted, however, that Singapore’s growth outlook is unlikely to be affected by this.

Economists have kept their non-oil domestic export (NODX) 2027 forecasts for the country unchanged, with some noting how the impact should be “relatively contained”.

Meanwhile, Vietnam was also upgraded to “overweight” by the JPMorgan analysts, from a “neutral” rating previously, due to monetary easing after a tightening phase.

“Corporate earnings would be underpinned by a ramp-up in public infrastructure investment and strong economic momentum,” they wrote.

Vietnam’s most recent structural reforms, “Doi Moi 2.0”, began in late 2024 and include construction of the country’s new International Financial Centre, and various transport and energy partnerships.

A year of two halves

Although JPMorgan forecasts a volatile H1 2027, it expects improvement in H2.

“Silver linings” could appear in the second half, especially when the need to diversify from artificial intelligence plays picks up, as market sentiment becomes more selective in 2027.

Fluctuating energy prices could be a catalyst, too.

“While the Middle-East situation outlook remains limited, alternative supply and sustained reduction in oil demand is bringing the oil market back to a surplus and points to lower oil prices in 2027,” the analysts wrote.

Such circumstances will offer significant support to Asean’s current account flows and ease inflationary pressures “materially”, they added.

Brent oil prices are set to decline to US$55 per barrel by end-2027, according to JPMorgan’s commodities team.

data.title: China’s industrial profit growth fastest in five months as recovery remains uneven
data.description:
[BEIJING] Profit growth at China’s industrial firms accelerated in October to the fastest in five months, supported by improving conditions in parts of the manufacturing sector, although broader economic momentum remained subdued.

The industrial profits data are closely watched as a gauge of corporate health, investment appetite and the effectiveness of Beijing’s stimulus measures. The figures also offer clues on whether stronger earnings could reduce pressure for further policy easing.

Profits at industrial firms rose 20.1 per cent from a year earlier last month, versus a 14.4 per cent gain in September, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Friday (Nov 27).

Profits were up 16 per cent in the first 10 months, accelerating from a 15.5 per cent increase in the January-September period.

But the breakdown highlighted a widening divergence across sectors.

Profit growth in AI-related industries and upstream sectors is outpacing that of downstream industries, while external demand remains an important source of support, said Ding Meng, Citic Bank International’s chief China economist.

The bureau’s data showed that profits in computer, telecommunications and other electronic equipment manufacturing doubled in the first 10 months, while furniture manufacturing posted a decline of 52.4 per cent.

“The recovery remains uneven and provides a more mixed signal on the health of the broader economy,” said Lynn Song, ING’s Greater China chief economist.

Broader Chinese indices were muted while tech stocks rebounded strongly. The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index jumped more than 5 per cent, while the Hang Seng Tech Index was up 3 per cent.

The disparity underscores the challenges facing policymakers as domestic demand remains weak and continues to weigh on large parts of the corporate sector.

Many manufacturers have increasingly relied on overseas sales to sustain growth, leaving them exposed to rising trade frictions and geopolitical risks.

Beijing has rolled out a series of support measures in recent months, including interest-rate cuts, liquidity injections and targeted financing support for sectors such as technology, manufacturing and infrastructure.

Still, analysts say the impact has been mixed, with weak household demand and lingering strains in the property sector continuing to drag on the broader recovery.

“The robust pace of profit growth further reinforces expectations that there will be no additional monetary policy easing in the near term,” Ding said.

The outlook for exports, a key source of support for manufacturers this year, has also become less certain. Concern over potential tariff increases and other trade restrictions, particularly in the United States and the European Union, has raised questions about the sustainability of export-driven growth.

Looking ahead, a potential slowdown in AI data centre investment, concerns over AI-sector profitability and leverage, and the risk of further Western restrictions on Chinese exports mean that “boosting domestic demand as soon as possible remains the key to sustaining profit growth,” Ding said.

Industrial profit figures cover firms with annual revenue of at least 20 million yuan (US$3 million) from main operations. BLOOMBERG

data.title: JPMorgan, BlackRock, Endowus frontrunners in scheme to lift returns on S$700 billion of CPF savings
data.description:
JPMORGAN Asset Management, BlackRock and Endowus Singapore are the frontrunners to manage a slice of Singapore’s S$701 billion (US$543 billion) public pension fund.

The three firms submitted proposals to run a new investment programme that offers an alternative for members of the Central Provident Fund who want to earn more than the government-guaranteed return, according to people familiar with the matter.

The winners will be announced in the first half of 2027. Discussions are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters.

JPMorgan would partner with Singapore’s largest bank, DBS, in an extension of a retirement portfolio programme that was piloted in 2024. Endowus, an investment platform, is in talks to work with Capital Group on the CPF programme, said the people.

A spokesperson for the CPF Board said the evaluation process is ongoing, and it can’t comment on individual applications.

JPMorgan and Capital Group declined to comment. Endowus said it has been a digital adviser for investing CPF savings since 2019. BlackRock and DBS didn’t respond to requests for comment.

The investment plan was unveiled by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in this year’s budget speech as a way to deal with the country’s aging population, and will be launched in 2028.

The new programme will allow members to opt in to portfolio strategies that automatically adjust according to their age. As investors get older, the equity allocation will shift to lower-risk assets such as bonds, before being liquidated in phases by a set target date.

Currently, members have the option of manually picking investments, including bonds, stocks and unit trusts, from a list of more than 30 asset managers. As of September, just S$22 billion – or 3 per cent – of net assets were invested in this optional plan, according to the CPF website.

The bulk of CPF savings are invested by the pension board in Special Singapore Government Securities. Proceeds from these securities are pooled with other government funds, including from budget surpluses and land sales, and managed by sovereign wealth fund GIC for long-term returns. Members under 55 earn risk-free interest of up to 5 per cent a year.

Founded in 1955, the CPF is Singapore’s mandatory pension fund for citizens and permanent residents to support retirement, housing and health-care needs. There are more than two million active members, and over S$14 billion in CPF contributions were received in the third quarter. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Asean must counter economic nationalism with deeper integration, wider partnerships: DPM Gan
data.description:
[SINGAPORE] Asean must counter rising economic nationalism with deeper integration and wider partnerships, in a world where governments are placing more emphasis on self-reliance and control over critical industries, said Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong on Nov 27.

“Raising barriers among ourselves would narrow the opportunities available to each of us,” he said. A more integrated Asean would strengthen its value as a partner, while broader tie-ups open up more opportunities for the region.

Gan, who is also Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Trade), was delivering a keynote speech at SPH Media’s Asia Future Summit 2026, jointly presented by The Straits Times, The Business Times, Lianhe Zaobao, Berita Harian and Tamil Murasu.

The annual event gathered policymakers, business leaders and industry experts, with OCBC as the presenting sponsor, Marina Bay Sands as the official venue partner and Amazon Web Services as the official cloud partner.

In his speech, Gan identified three factors that make integration and partnerships especially important: artificial intelligence, geopolitical shocks and geo-economic contestation. “Each can strengthen the impulse to turn inward. Yet each also makes cooperation more crucial,” he said.

His remarks followed the United States’ announcements of fresh tariffs and chip export restrictions over the past two weeks, moves which affected many in South-east Asia as the region finds itself in the crosshairs of sharpening rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

“Geo-economic competition is reshaping the networks through which we trade, invest and access technology,” Gan said, with governments paying closer attention to dependencies and control over critical capabilities.

“Asean countries cannot determine how major powers manage their differences,” he added. “But we can maintain relationships across these divides and remain a bridge for trade, investment and cooperation.”

Doing so would require that Asean earn and sustain its partners’ confidence in the grouping’s integrity, institutional reliability and business environment by issuing clear and predictable rules, upholding its laws and commitments, and taking firm action against wrongdoing, he said.

“As scrutiny of international trade and investment intensifies, maintaining these standards becomes even more important,” he added.

ASEAN will mark its 60th anniversary in 2027, with Singapore pushing for deeper integration and wider partnerships as it takes on Asean’s rotating chairmanship at a time of heightened geopolitical contestation.

Both the US and China would continue to be key economic partners for Asean, Gan said, with their businesses, technologies and markets important to the region’s growth.

Both countries are among the region’s largest trading partners and sources of foreign direct investment.

In tandem, the grouping is strengthening tie-ups with other partners that would expand the region’s economic options and reduce its exposure to disruptions, Gan said.

These include negotiations to upgrade Asean’s trade agreements with South Korea and Canada, moves to expand and enhance the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, and growing links with other regional groupings such as the European Union and Gulf Cooperation Council.

Asean is also strengthening integration within the grouping, with Gan highlighting recent efforts that would help firms better tap suppliers and customers within the region.

A recently upgraded Asean Trade in Goods Agreement, set to be rolled out in end-2026, will help businesses reduce costs through streamlined procedures and more transparent rules, he said, while a customs-related mutual recognition arrangement would give trusted traders faster clearances and priority treatment in participating countries.

And a regional Digital Economy Framework Agreement signed earlier in the month would make cross-border transactions, payments and access to digital services easier, he added.

These would make Asean more valuable as a place to produce and market to serve, and form a stronger regional base enabling the grouping to “engage the world with greater confidence”, Gan said. THE STRAITS TIMES

data.title: Bank of Japan calls for safeguards against digital money, AI risks
data.description:
[TOKYO] Global policymakers must strengthen defences against financial stability and cybersecurity risks posed by the emergence of new forms of digital money and financial infrastructure, Bank of Japan executive director Kazushige Kamiyama said on Friday (Nov 26).

New forms of digital money, such as stablecoins and tokenised deposits, are likely to co-exist and interact, which poses fresh challenges for policymakers such as ensuring the diversity does not create unnecessary fragmentation or undermine financial stability, he said.

The growing use of AI also brings fresh cybersecurity risks, requiring authorities and institutions to strengthen their defences against the growing ability of AI to discover and exploit vulnerabilities, Kamiyama said.

“My central message is that technological innovation offers significant opportunities to improve money and payments, but innovation must go hand in hand with trust,” Kamiyama said in a speech at the International Monetary Fund’s seminar on digital money and payments in Tokyo.

“Central bank money will continue to play a fundamental role as the anchor of trust in the monetary system,” he said.

Tokenisation is the process of turning assets such as bonds, deposits and securities into digital tokens that can be traded and settled on programmable platforms.

Policymakers globally are increasingly moving beyond experiments toward establishing rules and infrastructure for wider use, while seeking to ensure tokenised finance remains in the realm of regulated money and traditional financial system.

By creating new channels of trading across institutions and markets, tokenisation may amplify market movements during times of stress, Kamiyama said, citing it among risks that warrant vigilance.

Interconnected platforms may also allow cyber incidents to spread quickly, meaning new platforms must be designed with security and resilience from the outset, he said.

Beyond technological challenges, policymakers must create legal frameworks to clarify whether the transfer of a token effectively transfers legal rights and obligations in the underlying asset, Kamiyama said.

“Taken together, these challenges show that the benefits of tokenisation depend not on technology alone, but also on sound institutional arrangements, clear legal frameworks, and public-private cooperation,” he said. BLOOMBERG
